references.text: God's command to build the tabernacle (mishkan) according to the pattern shown to Moses on the mountain.
Detailed instructions for building the tabernacle, now being accounted for.
The tablets of testimony given to Moses, which gave the tabernacle the name 'tabernacle of testimony'.
The Levites' service at the tabernacle of testimony, their responsibility to carry and guard it.
The service of the Gershonites under the leadership of Ithamar, son of Aaron.
The service of Merari's sons under the leadership of Ithamar, the priest.
The tabernacle of testimony as the place where God spoke to Moses.
Ithamar's lineage as Aaron's son, mentioned in this overview.
Ithamar is mentioned together with his brother Eleazar after the death of Nadab and Abihu.
Complementary accounts: Exodus documents the accounting basis for the dwelling, while Numbers describes the actual inauguration of the service that was funded.
Execution by command: Exodus shows the Levites at work, while Numbers 1:50 establishes the divine arrangement that assigned them responsibility for the dwelling.
Task and purpose: Exodus identifies the Levites as responsible for the dwelling, while Numbers 1:53 reveals the theological necessity of this arrangement to protect the congregation.
